text:
Samir Patel: quick question — we need a lightweight API contract for region-aware failover + data residency for tenant requests. Proposal: single header + three modes. thoughts?
Anna Chen: +1 on keeping it small. We already have X-Tenant-Region hint in the proxy. prefer not to add multiple new headers.
Leah Gomez: what are the semantics of each mode? esp. 'strict' vs 'prefer'. legal wants clarity on behavior when local capacity is exhausted.
Samir Patel: thinking values: strict | prefer | none. strict = must stay in resident region else return an error. prefer = try resident then failover. none = ignore residency.
Priya Rao: legal: for some EU customers 'must stay' is required. If we fail open we may violate contract. If strict -> return 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons when unavailable is acceptable to legal — we need audit fields.
Mike O'Neill: operationally, returning 451 will break apps that expect a response; some clients would rather get degraded model. We should support both behaviors via policy not just a boolean. Eg: strict:error vs strict:allow-degrade? but that's messy.
Anna Chen: agree with Samir to keep values small. Maybe 'strict' implies block, 'prefer' implies best-effort. If a customer needs degraded behavior they can set prefer and application handles it.
Leah Gomez: also surface where the request was routed from for observability. Add header X-Routed-From or similar so downstream knows.
ops-bot: recent-sim: failover-sim-2026-02-10 -> 2.3% of resident-strict tenants hit remote due to planned maintenance.
Samir Patel: ok actionable: API header = X-Residency: strict|prefer|none. Response for strict-failure -> 451 + body containing {"reason":"residency_unavailable","consent_ref": "<id>"}. Also add response header X-Routed-From when we route to non-resident region (for prefer).
Priya Rao: request audit fields: residency_policy, observed_region, routed_region (if any), consent_reference. Logs and access logs must include tenant id.
Mike O'Neill: runtime change: routing layer must check tenant metadata store -> if strict and local capacity=0 -> short-circuit 451. If prefer -> attempt resident queue with timeout 100ms then fallback to next region, and add X-Routed-From. We'll need metrics: residency_blocked, residency_routed, residency_error.
Anna Chen: small API example:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Residency: strict
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{ "input":"..." }
```
response when strict fail:
```
HTTP/1.1 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-abc123

{ "error":"residency_unavailable", "consent_ref":"escrow:eu-8372" }
```
response when prefer routed:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Routed-From: eu
X-Request-Id: r-xyz789
{ "output":"..." }
```
Leah Gomez: +1 on 100ms resident attempt window. Also we should expose a header X-Residency-Decision: strict-block | routed | local for telemetry.
Samir Patel: decision summary so far: implement X-Residency header with strict|prefer|none; strict failures -> 451; prefer -> best-effort with X-Routed-From and X-Residency-Decision headers; log audit fields and create metrics.
Priya Rao: legal to review proposed response body and consent token format. We also need a retention policy for consent_ref in logs (cc: security).
Mike O'Neill: action items: (1) runtime PR to add residency checks & 100ms resident window (2) API spec PR documenting headers + sample responses (3) console telemetry update (4) legal + security review. I'll own (1) and (3).
Anna Chen: I'll write spec doc + examples.
Priya Rao: I'll follow up with legal review by EOD Wed.
Samir Patel: thanks — we should also add an integration test that simulates resident capacity exhaustion and validates 451 vs routed behavior.
ops-bot: scheduled-task: residency-integration-test added to ci/integration with tag residency-failover.
Leah Gomez: small follow: we should guarantee idempotency semantics unchanged; when we short-circuit with 451 we must not create any side effects. Document that.
Samir Patel: noted. final: can folks ack? :thumbsup:
Anna Chen: :thumbsup:
Leah Gomez: :thumbsup:
